The entire building is approximately 17,000 ft2 and individual units are approximately 480 ft2 in size. The apartments serve as low-income senior housing, and host 2 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. residents from the Fairbanks area, as well as surrounding towns that do not have senior housing. Built approximately 30 years ago in the 1990s, the building currently lacks many energy efficiency measures that are available today that can reduce energy costs for building owners and improve comfort for residents. 3.1 Lighting Lighting in the building is mostly T8 linear fixtures with Light Emitting Diode (LED) lamps in common areas and offices, with high-intensity discharge (HID) lamps outside. In individual units, the lighting consists of one T8 fixture with fluorescent lamps and two other fixtures with LED lamps, and a vanity fixture with LED lamps in bathrooms. 3.2 Heating The heating system for space heating and domestic hot water is a Burnham natural gas boiler, model # V904A, additionally with a Power Flame Burner, model # C1-GO-10, with conversion completed and the new heating system commissioned in October 2023, with an outdoor reset controller and baseboard distribution system. The domestic hot water system has a recirculation control that is on during business hours. There is no cooling system in the building. The thermostats are manual and located in each building zone. 3.3 Building Envelope Windows are triple panes with vinyl frames and original to the building (see Figure 5). The exterior walls and roof are in poor condition with the siding deteriorating in places (see Figure 6). The current windows include some that are double casements and others that are single casement. Residents have complained about windows being leaky and letting in cold drafts and icing up in the winter indicating that the glazing seals may be past their useful life.
